title: VP Science, Google DeepMind and Chief Scientist, Google Cloud
bio: Pushmeet Kohli is Vice President, AI for Science at Google DeepMind & Google Cloud’s Chief Scientist. He founded and leads the AI for Science and Strategic Initiatives Unit, which uses AI for breakthroughs in biology, materials, fusion, math, software, and cybersecurity. Key achievements include the Nobel Prize-winning AlphaFold model for protein structure prediction, one of the most cited AI biology papers (50,000+ citations).

title: Co-Founder & Chief Scientist
bio: I am a Co-Founder and Chief Scientist of Recursive and a Professor of AI at University College London (UCL). I am also faculty at the British Open-Ended Learning & Discovery (BOLD) national UK AI research lab, and a Fellow at the European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS). Before, I was a Director, Principal Scientist, and the Open-Endedness Team Lead at Google DeepMind, and before that the Reinforcement Learning Team Lead at Meta AI (FAIR) London.

title: VP of Research
bio: Zoubin Ghahramani is VP at Google DeepMind co-leading Frontier AI, as well as Professor of Information Engineering at the University of Cambridge. Before joining Google, he was Chief Scientist and VP for AI at Uber. He co-founded Geometric Intelligence (acquired by Uber) and was founding Cambridge Director of the Alan Turing Institute, the UK’s national institute for data science and AI.

s.title: Keynote

title: Partner Research Manager
bio: Katja Hofmann is a Partner Research Manager at Microsoft. Her work focuses on generative AI, interactive media, and game intelligence. Her long term goal is to unlock machine learning insights that enable AI systems to empower people in addressing complex real-world challenges.

s.title: Keynote

title: AI Research Lead
bio: Leon Chlon is AI Research Lead at PhysicsX, building in-context learning world models that predict physical fields from a handful of simulations, without retraining. He trained in theoretical physics and machine learning at Cambridge (MPhil, PhD) and did a postdoc at Harvard Medical School and MIT. He then built AI systems at McKinsey, Meta, Uber, Apple and TikTok before a Visiting Fellowship in Oxford's Torr Vision Group.

title: Director of AI
bio: Vassia Simaiaki is passionate about taking research into application and has spent the last decade of her career in computer vision and deep learning. She leads AI research and development at Wayve, focusing on pushing the boundaries of generative simulation and world modelling continuing to accelerate the driving performance and evaluation of autonomous vehicles.

title: Assistant Professor
bio: Oana-Maria Camburu is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computing at Imperial College London and a Principal Research Fellow in the Department of Computer Science at the University College London, where she previously held an Early Career Leverhulme Fellowship. She obtained her PhD in “Explaining Deep Neural Networks” from the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford.

title: Partner
bio: Eric is a partner in Cooley’s UK emerging companies and venture capital team. He advises high-growth technology companies and their investors on private financings, M&A and strategic and corporate governance matters, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence companies.

s.title: Panel: How to build a world-class AI research lab

title: CEO
bio: Danyal Akarca is Co-founder and CEO of Callosum, a London-based AI infrastructure company building heterogeneous compute orchestration for AI inference workloads. Callosum was the first company backed by the UK Sovereign AI fund and recently raised a $100m seed round. Danyal holds a PhD from the University of Cambridge and was previously a Schmidt Fellow in Electrical Engineering at Imperial College London.

s.title: Keynote

title: AI Safety
bio: Artemis Seaford is an AI safety and tech policy expert who has shaped safety practices at frontier AI companies. She most recently led AI Safety at ElevenLabs, establishing safety protocols to prevent voice cloning abuse and enable secure enterprise deployment of generative audio models. Previously at OpenAI, she designed and enforced usage policies for ChatGPT as it scaled to 100M+ users.

title: Distinguished Professor of Computer Science
bio: Stuart Russell is a Distinguished Professor of Computer Science at the University of California at Berkeley, holder of the Smith-Zadeh Chair in Engineering, and Director of the Center for Human-Compatible AI and the Kavli Center for Ethics, Science, and the Public.

title: Managing Partner
bio: Carles is an operator-turned-investor. He has been building and investing in companies for the past 15 years. He was an early International employee at Uber (NYSE: UBER), helped Tractable AI (unicorn) expand globally managing teams in London (HQ), NY, Austin TX and Tokyo, and built the Revenue side at Sonantic (acq by Spotify). He was also the first investor in ElevenLabs and the 4th employee, where he built the GTM globally.

title: Founder / CEO
bio: I'm the founder of Cursive, an applied AI lab in London spun out of DeepMind focused on post-training research. I am also an angel investor and founder of Clay Ventures, which has been investing in early-stage startups since 2021. I am also Welsh and passionate in how the UK should be adapting to progress in AI and technology.

title: Co-Founder & CEO at TesterArmy
bio: Szymon Rybczak is the co-founder and CEO of TesterArmy, YCP26. Szymon has been writing production code since he was 14 and became the youngest-ever contributor to React Native. Within two weeks of releasing e2e, the product has already passed 10k+ GitHub stars and 500k+ package downloads.

title: CO FOUNDER AND PARTNER
bio: Scott Sage is co-founder and Partner at Crane, where he's spent 15+ years working with exceptional founders. He invests across the full stack, drawn to teams tackling hard problems with conviction and craft. Scott's approach is guided by Crane's Meridian Principle: the belief that human progress accelerates when extraordinary people connect ideas across disciplines.

bio: I help shape how emerging technologies will support the BBC’s mission to inform, educate and entertain for the next century. I advise on strategic technology decisions, industry standards, and the social, editorial and ethical implications of innovation.

title: Managing Partner
bio: Suzanne is one of the UK's most respected venture investors. As a former General Partner at LocalGlobe and Latitude, she has spent a decade backing founders who have come to define a generation of British technology, including Tessian and Open Cosmos. She also co-authored the UK Tech Competitiveness Study, which recommended measures to close the digital skills gap, harness data and AI for public good, and strengthen regional tech ecosystems.

title: Director SOFAIR Lab
bio: David Barber received a BA in Mathematics from Cambridge University and subsequently a PhD in Theoretical Physics (Statistical Mechanics) from Edinburgh University. He is Director of the UKRI Science of Fundamental AI Research Lab (SOFAIR). He has broad research interests related to the application of probabilistic modelling and reasoning.

title: Investor
bio: Erwann is a investor at Sov/AI, where he backs exceptional scientists and technologists building ambitious companies in the UK at the frontiers of AI. He trained across medicine, biomedical engineering and robotics before completing a PhD focused on reinforcement learning and decision-making under uncertainty. Before Sov/AI, he spent 3.5 years helping build the venture team at XTX Markets and is also a research scientist at the AI Security Institute.

title: CTO
bio: Phil leads technology development at the intersection of genomics, AI, and bioinformatics. He studied Molecular Biology and Genetics at Oxford, later working in AI-driven drug discovery and teaching bioinformatics. Before Basecamp Research, he developed transcriptomic tools to discover new genes.

title: Strategic Partnerships Manager
bio: Lottie works in partnerships and strategy at Basecamp Research, with experience spanning human and planetary sciences. Previously, she conducted her PhD in cancer immunotherapy at King’s College London, whilst serving as London Managing Director at Nucleate UK and led its climate biotech programme, Eco, supporting early-stage founders. At the heart of her work is a passion for bringing people together to catalyse innovation and turn scientific ideas into practical impact.

title: Advisor & Investor
bio: Dr Tonya Frolov is a biologist, strategist and angel investor who works with biotech founders on positioning, investor communications and fundraising strategy. She was one of the earliest employees at bit.bio, where she helped scale the company past 180 people, held investor-facing roles at LabGenius through its Series B, then served as Strategy Director at Bunsen, a creative studio for biotech and deep tech startups, and has advised 40+ startups and VCs.
